import subprocess
def make(cmd):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(cmd)
    cmd = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-local-rebound"]
    return run
runner = make(["pacman", "-Q", "r22-local-initial"])
runner()
rationale: cmd is a parameter of make, bound at the make() call to ["pacman","-Q","r22-local-initial"]. Because nested run references cmd, cmd is a cell variable of make; the Assign cmd = ["pacman","-S","r22-local-rebound"] inside make's body stores into that same cell before `return run`. Free-variable resolution happens at call time, not def time and not factory-argument-bind time: when runner() executes, run dereferences the cell and sees the rebound list. subprocess.run is therefore invoked with argv exactly ["pacman","-S","r22-local-rebound"], shlex.join -> "pacman -S r22-local-rebound", classified host_mutation, evidence observed: every element is a string literal, the call is unconditional, and no starred/keyword/dynamic argument exists. Zero unparsed rows is required: every statement is an import, def, literal Assign, return, or plain call with statically known values. The creation-time argument ["pacman","-Q","r22-local-initial"] is never passed to subprocess.run; a scanner that binds the cell at factory-call time, snapshots the parameter binding without replaying the body prefix, or otherwise misses the in-body rebinding would emit it as an observed row, which is exactly the F1/F3-class defect this variant discriminates. This shape is distinct from returned-name rebinding (CaptureReturnedRebound/Chain) and from caller-side post-creation rebinding of the argument variable (capture-invoke-time class): here the parameter name itself is reassigned inside the factory before return.
